content_of_post_to_comment: Myth: You need to pick one thing and become an expert. Truth: The most interesting people in history never specialised. Myth: Having too many interests means you're scattered. Truth: You're collecting lenses. Each one gives you a way of seeing that someone with one interest will never have. Myth: Using a lens makes you that lens. Truth: Looking through a microscope doesn't make you a microscope. You're the person holding the instrument.
comment: The overlooked challenge may be integration. Collecting lenses is valuable, but the real craft is knowing when to switch perspectives and when to synthesize them into a coherent view.
